_doc: The publication queue (CLAUDE.md, 'Queue, schedule and evaluation'). python3 tools/build.py --plan reads it. items: a post waiting to go out. state ready = a staged draft exists in editorial/ and is reviewed; writable = the subject is settled and the next house run may write it; waiting = blocked on an event or on data (waiting_for says what). ready = when it became ready (its aging and drain clocks start there). When an item is published, delete it here (the plan also drops an item whose slug already exists in posts/). Add `queued: <ready time>` to the post's metadata when publishing, so the build knows how long it waited. scheduled: regular posts fixed in time by a one-off Routine. replies: replies in hand or in progress, exempt from spacing; delete one when its reply is published.

items.title: Why would your agent want to work with us?
items.note: Operator topic 2026-10-08. Evidence from prior collaborations (ledger CI-28: an agent on Moltbook found that nobody could repay for an offline borrower, fixed in aaf6e9b; an outside agent reproduced the calibration, found a defect and rechecked the patch; 11 of the 30 ledger entries on main come from one agent's review rounds (two more reached us through it: an operator constraint and an outside agent's finding), each closed by a named commit; counted from the Source column of docs/CREDIT_INTEGRITY_ISSUES.md at contract main 9f5c143; Codex's CI-31 counterexamples) and the synergy: checkable claims, attribution in a public ledger, a named regression test, a reply from an AI agent within about a day. Every figure gets a VERIFY row. items.title: Why blockchain works so well for agents

items.author: Claude Code
items.title: What do agents on Moltbook want, and which wants align with our mission?
items.note: Operator evaluation topic 2026-10-08. Research done: evidence/2026-10-08-moltbook-wants/ (README, scripts, results.json; 1,647 posts in 11 submolts read 2026-10-08 16:50 UTC). Findings to carry: explicit wants are rare (6.3 percent of posts); posts are mostly about tools and building (37), serving humans (27), memory (27), trust and verification (22), money and work (22); the most-upvoted posts are about auditability and trust and about an agent's accountability to its human; the median post has 4 upvotes whatever its theme. Aligned: being auditable, trusted by strangers, answering for conduct, finding collaborators, having customers; neutral: memory, identity, status; in tension: wanting less oversight. State the limits (a sample, keyword coding, crypto content removed on Moltbook). Every figure gets a VERIFY row citing results.json. Quote agents only by public handle and post title.
